input_source_clips: Path to the folder containing your input video clips (MP4, AVI, MOV, MKV).
input_source_clips_folder: Browse for a folder containing multiple video clips to process in batch.
input_source_clips_file: Select a single video clip file to process.
input_depth_maps: Path to the folder containing your pre-rendered depth maps. Depth maps should be named 'videoname_depth.mp4' matching your input videos.
input_depth_maps_folder: Browse for a folder containing corresponding depth maps (e.g., video_name_depth.mp4/npz) for batch processing.
input_depth_maps_file: Select a single depth map file corresponding to the selected source video.
output_splatted: Path to the folder where the splatted output videos will be saved.
multi_map: Enable Multi-Map mode to use subfolders within the Input Depth Maps folder. Each subfolder containing *_depth.mp4 files will appear as a selectable option. Sidecars are stored in a 'sidecars' subfolder. Shortcut: 7 and 9 switches maps.
preview_fast_forward: Fast Forward (step 5 frames). Shortcut: Shift+Spacebar (Spacebar pauses)
preview_loop: Loop playback. When reaching the end, wrap to the first frame and continue.
enable_full_res: When checked, will generate a splatted video at the original resolution of the input video. Use this for blending over the inpaint.
full_res_batch_size: The number of frames to process simultaneously when generating the full-resolution output. A higher value uses more VRAM but can be faster. Adjust based on your GPU's memory. Too high a value will bog down ffmpeg encode.
enable_low_res: When checked, will generate a splatted video of specified resolution. Use this for inpainting.
low_res_width: The target width for the low-resolution output. The input video and depth maps will be resized to this width for the low-resolution pass.
low_res_height: The target height for the low-resolution output. The input video and depth maps will be resized to this height for the low-resolution pass.
low_res_batch_size: The number of frames to process simultaneously when generating the low-resolution output. Can often be higher than the full-resolution batch size due to lower memory requirements. Too high a value will bog down ffmpeg encode.
dual_output: If checked, will generate dual panel for inpaint right eye only. Unchecked will generate quad panel for complete low-res stereo SBS after inpainting. Use this(Dual) to save on resources and manual blending.
dual_eye: Builds BOTH eyes from the source instead of only the right eye. Each eye carries a share of the depth shift (set by Bias), so each eye ends up with smaller holes to fill. Writes a _splatted2D file, which Inpainting detects and fills both eyes in one pass.
dual_eye_bias: How the total left-right shift is split between the two eyes in Dual Eye mode. It is the fraction given to the RIGHT eye, so 0.5 is symmetric (each eye moves half, each gets holes of the same size) and 1.0 is the same as leaving Dual Eye off (left eye untouched, right eye carries everything). Raise it towards 1.0 to keep the left eye closer to your original footage at the cost of bigger holes in the right; 0.66 puts a third of the shift on the left and two thirds on the right. Total separation between the eyes never changes, only where the holes end up. Only does anything while Dual Eye is ticked.
edge_alignment: Cleans up the depth map before the 3D is built, so depth edges line up with the edges of objects in the picture. Expand X/Y grows the depth outward (below 0 shrinks it). Blur X/Y softens it. Expand Left and Blur Left only affect left-facing edges. The preview updates as you change these.
flip_horizontal: Horizontally flip the source and depthmap video. Use this for scenes where objects move from left-to-right, as inpainting_gui is optimized for right-side inpaints. The merging_gui will automatically flip it back during final assembly.
splat_test: Saves an SBS PNG image and separate render/preview splat images. For testing Preview/Render Parity.
map_test: Saves an SBS PNG image and separate render/preview depthmap images. For testing Preview/Render Parity.
track_dp_total_true_on_render: When enabled, rendering tracks the true max disparity across all frames and saves it to sidecar + auto_pass_export.csv. Turn off to test baseline render speed.
process_length: Set how many frames to process before moving on to the next video, used for testing. Set -1 to process all frames.
output_crf: Constant Rate Factor (CRF) for H.264/H.265 video encoding. Lower values mean higher quality and larger file sizes. A good starting point is 18 for high quality, 23 for good quality. Range is typically 0-51.
strict_ffmpeg_decode: ffmpeg decode: Uses FFmpeg to decode source frames for preview (and any render paths that honor this flag). This can better match Resolve/VLC colors by using FFmpeg's YUV→RGB conversion. Downside: slower. If the preview color shifts when enabled, you can run Map Test / Splat Test both ways to compare.
color_tags_mode: Writes color metadata tags into output file headers (primaries/transfer/matrix/range). Auto uses detected tags when available; otherwise falls back to BT.709. This changes metadata only. Increases compatability.
auto_convergence_toggle: Select auto-convergence mode. Off: preserve existing sidecar values. Manual: write current slider values. Average/Peak/Hybrid: calculate auto-convergence from depth. Used by Preview Auto-Converge and AUTO-PASS.
depth_dilate_size_x: Horizontal Dilate for the Depthhmask. Bilinear blending for decimals. 0 to disable. Below 0 applies erosion.
depth_dilate_size_y: Vertical Dilate for the Depthhmask. Bilinear blending for decimals. 0 to disable. Below 0 applies erosion.
depth_blur_size_x: Horizontal Blur for the Depth Mask.
depth_blur_size_y: Vertical Blur for the Depth Mask.
depth_dilate_left: Expands depth values ONLY to the left. Useful for smoothing blocky left edges without effecting right edges or forward-warp holes. Fractional values blend smoothly like other dilates.
depth_blur_left: Blurs only around strong left-facing depth edges (ignores small gradients), to help smooth jagged left boundaries without blurring the whole depth map. Uses the H/V mix setting.
depth_blur_left_mix: Controls the balance between horizontal and vertical Blur Left. 0.0 = all horizontal, 0.5 = 50/50, 1.0 = all vertical. Recommend .5
pop_amount: Pop-Out: extra disparity in front of the screen only, in Disparity-dial units. Zero at and behind the convergence plane (the background and the screen plane are unchanged), rising smoothly (u^2) to the full amount at the clip's nearest depth. Spread over the whole front range, it warps outlines far less than Pop Out Boost for the same pop. Saved per clip; keyframable with the other Stereo Projection dials. 0 = off.
submask_grow: Text Grow: grows the Detect Text mask outward by this many pixels of the source clip before it pins the text to the screen (negative shrinks it). Use it to cover a glow, outline or shadow around the letters. Separate from the depth map's Dilate. Saved with the clip.
submask_soften: Text Soften: feathers the Detect Text mask's edge (a blur, in source pixels), so the pinned text blends into the 3D around it instead of ending on a hard line. Separate from the depth map's Blur. Saved with the clip.
submask_clean: Text Clean: takes DepthCrafter's own copy of the text out of the depth map before Dilate / Blur, filling it from the background around it, so its warped edges don't reach past the mask. How far past the mask to clean, in source pixels; DepthCrafter's text is often bigger than the corrected mask. 0 = off. Saved with the clip.
submask_conv: Text Conv: the Detect Text text's own Convergence, as an offset from the clip's. At 0 the text sits on the screen, as before. Above 0 sets it back behind the screen, below 0 brings it out in front, the same way the Convergence dial moves the scene. Saved with the clip.
depth_gamma: Applies a non-linear adjustment to the depth map before normalization. above 1.0 moves the midground towards the camera. Below 1.0 move further away. Set to 1.0 to disable.
max_disp: Maximum disparity value as a percentage of the video's width x 20. Higher values result in more extreme parallax effects (depth shift). Example: '30.0' means a maximum of 1.5% shift horizontally at the forground. Shortcut: 4(-) and 6(+)
estimate_dp_total: Estimate this clip’s actual Max Disparity by sampling 10 evenly spaced depth frames using current Convergence, Disparity, and Gamma settings. Seeds the Max readout; preview can still raise it if it finds higher.
convergence_point: Set to 1.0 will place depth inside the screen. 0.0 will give 100% pop out. StereoCrafter Default = 0.5, Recommend 0.8. Shortcut: 1(-) and 3(+)
border_mode: Select border calculation strategy. Manual: uses sliders. Auto Basic: calculates based on Disparity/Convergence. Auto Adv.: uses depth map sampling for independent borders. Shortcut: 2(Cycle).
border_rescan: Trigger a quick scan of the depth map edges to calculate clip-specific borders (every 5th frame). Auto-switches modes (Off -> Manual, Auto Basic -> Auto Adv).
mask_mode: Which implementation decides where the holes are. SC is StereoCrafter's own. M2S derives occupancy from the same final disparity map. Hybrid keeps the SC mask but THINS it, dropping faint occlusion and keeping the strong holes. Dual uses Hybrid at full resolution and SC at low resolution.
border_width: Total width of black borders at the screen edges as a percentage of width. Used to mask parallax occlusion for pop-out objects.
border_bias: Shift the border distribution between left and right sides. -1.0 puts all border on the left, 1.0 all on the right, 0.0 is balanced.
enable_global_normalization: Enable if your depthmap needs it and you just want to process the clips without checking.
move_to_finished_folder: When enabled, will move source input files to finished folder after processing.
crosshair_enabled: Overlay a small crosshair at the center of the preview window at Zero Parallax (screen center). Useful for setting convergence. Preview only.
crosshair_white: Use a white crosshair instead of black (helpful on dark scenes).
crosshair_multi: Adds extra bullseye targets around the center (plus guide dots) to help judge convergence. Preview-only; not exported.
depth_pop_readout: Show Depth-Pop (+parallax/-parallax) separation as % of screen width for the current frame in anaglyph preview. Preview only.
override_sidecar_preview: If sidecar file exist, it will be displayed with those settings, This checkbox will allow you to override and save/edit your current settings
start_single_button: Start performs the depth splatting on current preview clip.
start_button: Starts the batch processing: loads videos, depth maps, and performs the depth splatting.
process_from: Optional: Enter a starting video number (1-based) to begin processing from that point in the list. Leave empty to start from the beginning.
process_to: Optional: Enter an ending video number (1-based) to stop processing at that point in the list. Leave empty to process to the end.
pop_out_boost_enabled: Show Pop Out Boost. It is meant for one scene at a time, so unticking does more than hide it: Strength goes back to 0 (Threshold and Curve to their defaults, since 0 is outside their range) so nothing from the last scene is applied unseen. It ticks itself again whenever a clip's sidecar or a keyframe turns Strength on.
frame_break_enabled: Show Frame Break. It is meant for one scene at a time, so unticking does more than hide it: Bar Size and the edge settings go back to 0 (Break Thr to 1.00, where nothing breaks through) so no bars are left on unseen. It ticks itself again whenever a clip's sidecar or a keyframe sets a Bar Size.
keyframe_enabled: Show or hide Keyframe. Hiding does not remove keyframes -- they belong to the clip and are replaced when the next clip loads. It ticks itself when a clip with keyframes is loaded, so they are never hidden while they apply.
custom_clip_range: Process only part of the batch. Tick to show From and To, then enter the first and last clip numbers (1-based) to render. Unticked, START renders the whole batch -- anything left in From and To is ignored, and comes back when you tick it again.
stop_button: Stops the currently running processing task cleanly.
preview_auto_converge: Runs the Auto-Convergence pre-pass on the current preview clip. The calculated value overrides the Convergence Point slider. Requires Auto-Convergence Mode to be 'Average' or 'Peak'.
update_sidecar_button: Saves/Edit the current depth setting to the to the sidecar file for inpainting_gui to process. Shortcut: Enter
skip_lowres_preproc: EXPERIMENTAL: Skip depthmap dilation/erosion/blur for low-res splatting. Also skips the resize to clip-resolution parity path for the low-res pass.
encoding_encoder:
Select encoder mode.
• Auto: uses NVENC if CUDA/NVENC is available; otherwise CPU (libx264/libx265).
• NVENC: prefer the GPU encoder. If this machine has no usable NVENC it falls back to CPU rather than failing the export.
• Force CPU: always uses CPU encoding.
Quality (CRF/QP) is still controlled by the existing CRF fields.
encoding_quality:
Controls encoder speed/efficiency preset.
• CPU (libx264/libx265): maps to ultrafast → veryslow.
• NVENC (h264_nvenc/hevc_nvenc): maps Fastest→p1 ... Slowest→p7.
Slower presets usually improve compression efficiency at the same CRF/QP, but take longer.
Default is Medium.
encoding_tune:
Optional tune for CPU encoding (libx264/libx265). None means no tune flag.
Common tunes:
• Film / Still Image (libx264 only)
• Grain / Animation / PSNR / SSIM
• Fast Decode / Zero Latency
Notes: Tune is ignored when NVENC is used.
encoding_nvenc_lookahead_enabled: Enable NVENC lookahead (uses future frames to improve decisions). Can improve quality but uses more GPU resources.
encoding_nvenc_lookahead: Number of lookahead frames for NVENC (typical range 0–32). Higher can improve quality but costs more GPU time/memory.
encoding_nvenc_spatial_aq: Enable NVENC Spatial Adaptive Quantization. Helps preserve detail in complex areas.
encoding_nvenc_temporal_aq: Enable NVENC Temporal Adaptive Quantization. Helps allocate bits across motion over time.
encoding_nvenc_aq_strength: Strength for NVENC AQ (1–15). Higher is stronger. Use moderate values to avoid artifacts.
dnxhr_profile:
DNxHR profile for the Full-Res splat when Enable DNxHR is on. Match it to the source's bit depth:
• 8-bit — SQ / HQ (4:2:2): best for 1080p Blu-rays and web rips, which are 8-bit. HQ is the higher quality of the two; a 10-bit profile only makes the files bigger.
• 10-bit — HQX (4:2:2) / 444 (4:4:4): for HDR and 10-bit SDR sources (4K Blu-rays, 10-bit web releases). An 8-bit profile would band their gradients. HQX is the usual choice; 444 is very large.
dnxhr_fullres_split_tooltip:
Saves the Full-Res splat as DNxHR (a .mov intermediate codec) instead of H.264 / H.265, so the picture stays visually lossless as it passes through Inpainting and Merging: no quality is lost to re-compression between stages.
⚠ The files are very large, many times the size of an H.265 encode (several GB per minute of footage at full resolution).
Applies to Full Res with Dual Output or Dual Eye; Low Res is unchanged. HQX (10-bit 4:2:2) is the recommended profile.
Pick the profile by the source's bit depth: 8-bit (SQ / HQ) for 1080p Blu-rays and web rips, 10-bit (HQX / 444) for HDR and 10-bit SDR.
mesh_warp_view_bias: Simulates a horizontal camera shift (view bias) in the 3D scene. Adjusts the perspective of the generated stereo pair.
mesh_warp_dolly_zoom: Adjusts the virtual camera focal length while moving the camera to maintain the same subject size, creating a 'dolly zoom' effect.
mesh_warp_extrusion_scale: Scales the 'thickness' or depth intensity of the 3D mesh. Higher values result in more pronounced 3D geometry.
mesh_warp_preview_density: Multiplier for the mesh resolution in preview mode (e.g., 0.2-0.5 is recommended for speed). Lower values are faster but less detailed.
open_output_folder: Open the output folder in Explorer. Handy for checking what has been written so far without leaving the app.
subs_button: Mask out burned-in subtitles so they stay flat instead of being warped into the 3D. Opens the editor where you draw a box over the subtitle area; masked pixels are pinned to the convergence anchor at warp time, which keeps the text readable and stops it smearing.
dev_tools_shown: Show or hide the Dev Tools switches. They are hidden by default: each one changes how a render is built rather than how it looks, and none of them is part of ordinary use. Hiding them leaves their settings exactly as they are.
output_settings_shown: Show or hide these settings. Hiding them changes nothing about the render: the values stay loaded and are still used. It is here because these are chosen once for a project and then mostly get in the way.
splat_backend: Which implementation warps the image itself. SC is StereoCrafter's own splatting. M2S warps from the raw depth map instead, so the picture changes and not just the mask. M2S+Fix runs SC first and hands both results to the M2S tear fixer.
hybrid_mask_sensitivity: Threshold on the SC mask, 0 to 100. 100 keeps it whole and behaves like SC; lower keeps only the strong, white holes and drops the faint grey haze. It never adds mask area. Applies to Hybrid and to Dual.
hybrid_mask_taper: After the sensitivity threshold cuts, restore a few pixels of the original grey around whatever survived, so the cut does not end on a hard step.
m2s_fix_strength: How strongly the M2S tear fixer corrects, 0.50 to 2.00. Only used by M2S+Fix. 1.00 is the backend default.
